These are estimates from prior knowledge of NAS-Bench-201 behavior, not computed from the benchmark data. Most pairs are likely to show no consistent interaction, so I put most of the mass on N. I moved mass toward H or L where the structure suggests an interaction.

- **Edits that matter more when alternative paths are missing.** Setting edge 2 to a conv matters more when edge 1 or edge 5 is weak. Removing an edge hurts less when a strong parallel path exists.
- **Pairs where the condition replaces the edit's own edge.** Pair 0 (conv_1x1 replacing avg_pool on edge 0) and pair 16 (skip_connect replacing conv_3x3 on edge 4) have conditions that decide what the edit replaces. These carry larger effects.
- **Edits that cut connectivity.** Edge 0 is the main input path, so edits to it matter a lot. Setting edge 0 to none or skip_connect depends strongly on the other edges.
